proposals.relationship: Winter challenges Ferguson’s confident counterfactual account of British nonintervention in1914 as exceeding the available evidence.
proposals.evidence_note: Distinguishes projections from predictions and offers a defensive-war alternative. Praises economic, morale and surrender chapters. Ferguson disputes this reading in the reply.

proposals.relationship: Ferguson rejects Winter’s German-war-economy explanation and argues that Winter’s causal judgments themselves require counterfactuals.
proposals.evidence_note: Own reply contests Winter’s interpretation, including victory timing and stabilization. This is Ferguson’s attributed position; no book verification claimed.
primary_locators: Author response paragraphs beginning A core argument; I reject; Instead, Winter; This is a counsel; Winter also misrepresents.

proposals.relationship: Foner criticizes Colossus for presenting a sanitized account of American continental expansion that underplays military conquest.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2005 review explicitly names Colossus and contrasts Ferguson’s brief account with Fred Anderson and Andrew Cayton’s coauthored Dominion of War. Criticism targets the account’s impression of peaceful settlement and land purchase, not a claim that Ferguson denies all American empire. Foner’s later criticisms of Dominion’s biography structure, slavery omissions and internal roots are not reassigned to Ferguson. Original books unread.
primary_locators: Opening paragraph beginning Perhaps the leading current populariser; paragraph beginning Like Ferguson, Fred Anderson and Andrew Cayton.

proposals.relationship: Ferguson takes Weber’s Protestant-ethic thesis as a framework for examining the relationship between religion and economic development.
proposals.evidence_note: Own adapted2011 excerpt47 explains the thesis and48 retains a qualified positive argument about Protestant literacy, trust, saving and human capital. Its final reformulation emphasizes the word ethic. Substantial criticism coexists with this conceptual use: no complete assent, direct mentorship, or unqualified religious superiority claim inferred. Weber’s original essays and full Civilization unread.
primary_locators: Capitalist Calling printed47, opening and paragraph beginning When Weber returned;48 middle column Nevertheless and concluding right column.

proposals.relationship: Ferguson criticizes Weber’s evidence and causal account while retaining a qualified relationship between Protestantism and economic development.
proposals.evidence_note: Own48 identifies tensions in rational/irrational asceticism, Weber’s treatment of Jewish capitalism, overlooked Catholic entrepreneurs and inadequate comparative evidence. He then presents Tawney’s causal objection and an unnamed city study, before offering literacy/human-capital mechanisms. This is partial revision, not rejection of every Weberian proposition; neither unnamed study nor Tawney is falsely credited as Ferguson’s discovery. Originals unread.
primary_locators: Capitalist Calling printed48 left column Weber’s thesis is not without its problems through Later scholars;middle/right positive qualification.

proposals.relationship: Ferguson cites Tawney’s challenge to treating religious doctrine as the prior cause of capitalist economic behavior.
proposals.evidence_note: Own48 explicitly singles out R.H.Tawney among later scholars questioning Weber’s causal direction, then discusses pre-Reformation capitalist developments and anti-capitalist reformers. This is a named critical resource within Ferguson’s qualified argument; no exact Tawney title, edition or original passage supplied by the excerpt, and none invented. Tawney’s original unread.
primary_locators: Capitalist Calling printed48 left-column paragraph beginning Later scholars, notably the Fabian economic historian R.H.Tawney.

proposals.relationship: In Mähkä and Tringham’s account, Ferguson counters Thompson’s dismissal of counterfactual history by defending alternatives grounded in contemporary evidence.
proposals.evidence_note: Named substantive scholarly mediation: their Ferguson section reports Thompson among several critics cited in the1997 Introduction4–6 and presents Ferguson’s restricted plausible-alternatives argument85–89. He also criticizes frivolous and anachronistic scenarios12–20. This is a methodological disagreement, not a personal exchange or claim Thompson reviewed Ferguson; originals and original wording context unread. Carr,Croce and Oakeshott retain separate credit and missing-endpoint dispositions.
